After everything... thank you. We've barely met, but what you were just a part of has saved us all. You saw what we had to do. It was us, or them. The survivalists... We gave them thirty years to change their minds. We looked for a different way. Another outpost, maybe another abandoned radio station. Some other old colonial base. Anywhere. But everywhere we looked it was more untouched wilderness.

Those bloody fools. They wouldn't help us because they thought all those years ago when we crashed that we'd kill them in their sleep. They were always here before us, and so we begged for their aid. But they closed their gates to us. Innocents died because they wanted to ''cull the herd''. They kept to their small community and despised us for no good reason save that they would rather save themselves.

What choice did we have? They would not even send a message to colonial authorities, something that would be so incredibly easy for them to do. That, is how much they despised us from the beginning. How much they loathed us. Loathed everyone but themselves. They turned away from God and yet they wore the flesh of righteousness, labelling us as heretics that only deserved death on the end of their gun. They shot at us for decades if anyone dared cross their path.

And... their eyes... You saw it in their eyes! That zealotry! Fanaticism! Every single one of them, so indoctrinated by some bastardization of the Lord's teachings. And for what? Just so that we wouldn't touch their guns? So their radio wouldn't be captured? So they could keep living in filth?!

I have seen so many desperate people fall to just a handful of fanatics. All so our children could grow up to live amongst the stars again, and not on this desolate wilderness. This medieval life isn't romantic, nor glorious. We go every winter hoping we don't starve, and we pray the Brigands don't torch the villages.

The people now have something to hope for again. We won't be going quietly into the night, no longer. We'll keep on fighting, every day, until those ships take us home.

You know, I've never really met someone outside of my village. Always saw the same people, and not often would we see much of any travellers. Just the occasional brigand trying to steal or the few patrols that are still left to protect us. Even when we are safe, the harvest haven't been good the last few years. We've been eating through the grain stockpiles and meat is getting harder to come by. The elders say we still have a few years left, but Akeman Port is sending out reports that we have less if we can't secure what they call a ''trans-system radio station''.

Apparently, there's been a big call to rally all the military-men from all the villages to go on some sort of campaign. There's nothing that says against who, but my father thinks it's to wipe those brigands for good. Mother thinks differently though, and she says as long as there's people there'll always be criminals to feed on it, so it's something else. I don't know what it's all about, but I guess being sent out to do a supply run gives three of us an excuse to figure it out.
The brigands aren't scared of people. They'll keep fighting.

I think they've just got a death wish, missus. We've given them a good ol' beating plenty of times and sent them running, but... it's true that they always keep coming back. I've heard stories from the elders that crime like this was almost gone where they came from.

The elders always talk about what life was before all of this, and how so much better it was. How we took it for granted. How apparently you'd never run out of food and all you had to worry about was if your food was too hot or if your bath was too cold. I couldn't imagine such a life, and as much as I want to believe them... I think they're lying.

I mean, think about it. We came from a ship that could fly into the void above. Every ship I've been on has been this damp, wet, vessel. Always cramped too. Then they're going to tell me something like that held a million people or whatever because it just happened to be the size of a mountain. Then they tell us that this ship doesn't exist anymore because it all melted a million miles away in ''nuclear fire''. It's ridiculous, I tell you.

Pray tell me, mister. Are our hearts cold, or are we cold hearted? Why have we continued on like this? This violent reality where there is no joy and no life?

My grip on this reality... It is different. But I can still shift the tides. I have left something for you. Treasure it, and I will be right behind you.

As I have told you before, I'm a youkai. A Karakasa Obake. Technically not a human. I know... I look exactly like one. Most of our kind these days are not blind to that fact. Many of us did not choose this form.

I used to feed off the spiritual energies from people by... scaring them. Just... scaring them. Giving them a fright. Give a young kid a peekaboo or freak out some human, so long as it scared them I wouldn't go hungry. I didn't ask for that kind of existence, but that was what our Creator gave unto us.

It's hard to believe now, but people like Nazrin and I came from that once-flourishing kingdom. Both Man and Youkai were close to harmony with one-another, embracing each other for their strengths, and their weaknesses. The youkai feared humanity as much as humans within those lands feared youkai. It was almost a sort of mutual reverence. After all, a youkai cannot live without the spiritual energies that radiate passively from humanity... but yet, humans were so keen to find their purpose in that otherworld.

Life enchants us, to the point of fascination. It grants us an obsession to find purpose from the very beginning we are born. Both of us were brought to this realm, given life, but the means so different. Yet, does this make a spirit and a human so different? We live in this same realm, and in many ways... we need each other as much as we do the life that sustains us.

I was once a nobody in my home... Gensokyo, they would call it. For so long I thought that nobody loved me, but... I was blind to think such thoughts...

Even when others could see the value in me, I rejected that notion until they were gone.

Every one of them went into that starry void until naught but humanity was left. To fend against an enemy that despised them for no reason... None at all.

Ah...

Such fleeting moments... all of them. So many things are forgotten in the cosmic wind of time and space. Even that fiery humanity that fuels us all...

Yet you? You have been the worst of them. You blinded our kind into believing that they are better than us. That they should no longer fear us as they have for hundreds of years. You encourage them to rebel against us!

No longer are we free to feast on them. They hunt us down, and we are forced to conform to their rules. They now believe themselves as Gods over us, while you allow them to worship the false idol they call ''Christ''. When us youkai are no longer feared in these lands, when the cycle has broken, what then? We will be erased from this world.

[Momiji coughs up blood and begins to speak]

No. They accept us for who we are. Mankind embraces us as we have them. They have the spark to ignite Gensokyo into a new era of progress. When the sky burned seven years ago, we lost everything too! The world has already changed! We may be ageless, but we've known it for a long time now that death looms over all of us! The youkai can bleed now!

[Uragirimono speaks]

These... humans... they are nothing to us. They live for mere fractions of our lives and they wallow in selfishness and greed. They kill each other for petty trinkets and drink themselves to sleep every day. They have done nothing for us while we have made this world the way it is. We have kept peace, and if the price is a mere human, then so be it.

They are cattle to be herded and kept complacent as WE forge ahead.

[Momiji speaks]

They are the ones who built our cities. The ones who survived a nuclear genocide, and your genocide. It is their blood on our lands. They are the ones who have fed Gensokyo as we have lived in comfort our entire existence. It is the natural order that our time is ending, and the Age of Man begins.

But it seems like you are envious of them, like a child. How very human of you, Oni.

[Uragirimono speaks]

You filthy traitor.

You won't be talking filth out of your mouth when I put you into the void.

[Uragirimono reveals a talisman]

You know what this is? It's a little talisman with your name on it. I have sacrificed everything to Othniel's Pagans for this. I even had to find a piece of your hair for this. When I put this on you, it will remove you from this world as if you never existed. Your soul will never reach the heavens. But don't worry, you'll come back in a few hundred years. It'll be like you just went for a sleep.

And you will return to a Gensokyo without your cities or your kind. You will wander this world after we have restored the natural order of the youkai, and you will become nothing.

All I have to do... is just...

[Uragirimono forcefully applies the talisman onto Momiji's forehead]

Enjoy your sleep, traitor.

[Momiji disappears from the world...]

Sir, the city is ours. What should we do with them?
Take the heads of the men, youkai or not. I want the women alive.

So the two of you decided on it, yeah? More people always makes for a safer trip, so anyone trifling with us is gonna get a beatin'. Right, you two should get to know each other. We'll be on the road for about two days so long as nothing here goes wrong.

So, most people around here generally know who's who. Only peasants, bandits, and peasants who try to fight each other. No room for people doing merchant work. You two though? I don't think anyone's seen both of you before. All the villages 'round here know each other, because we're all family. You're both odd ones out here, but you're both not brigands, and you both don't have villages. But not like living in a village is very exciting. Most of the elders still talk tales of what it was like in the black void above.

My father says we're lucky to still be here. That we all came from a ship from above as part of one greater civilization, but now we're all just forgotten here. He says this should have never happened, and that it's a miracle that only twelve-thousand people could start a whole new life like this. I personally don't think it's much of a miracle, given that we're here, right? I've lived here all my life, and I don't think I'd have it any other way.

Just the occasional brigand trying to steal or the few patrols that are still left to protect us. Even when we are safe, the harvest haven't been good the last few years. We've been eating through the grain stockpiles and meat is getting harder to come by. The elders say we still have a few years left, but Akeman Port is sending out reports that we have less if we can't secure what they call a ''trans-system radio station''.

Apparently, there's been a big call to rally all the military-men from the all the villages to go on some sort of campaign. There's nothing that says against who, but my Father thinks it's to wipe those brigands for good. Mother thinks differently though, and she says as long as there's people there'll always be criminals to feed on it, so it's something else. I don't know what it's all about, but I guess being sent out to do a supply run gives both of us an excuse to figure it out.

The elders always talk about what life was before all of this, and how so much better it was. How we took it for granted. How apparently you'd never run out of food and all you had to worry about was if your food was too hot or if your bath was too cold. I couldn't imagine such a life, and as much as I want to believe them... I think they're lying.

Maybe you've figured already that this place is lawless and more technologically-regressed than you'd like, so I apologize for that. Brigands have been pushing our men harder than usual and it's been hard to keep everything in check.

Alright, look, you probably want to know what's going on. Our people have been stranded on this planet for about 30 years now. Passenger liner went boom onto the surface and apparently not a single bureaucrat could muster up a rescue effort. I don't think it takes a muppet to realize that passenger ships aren't exactly the pinnacle of self-sustainability, so that puts us back two thousands years of progress.

For thirty damned years we've been stuck on this rock living out some pretend-medieval age because that's all we had left. You can't make new bullets when there's no industry to support it, and you can't even start a new society when half the new generation lives on a life of crime. Most of our old gear don't work anymore. We're mostly down to crossbows and a handful of muskets. There's enough food to last us a few winters but our crops are dying out faster by the season.

Wasn't all as smooth as now either. When we first crashed here it was a mess. For a few days we thought our government would mount some sort of effort to pick us all up. A week goes by though and the rations we had onboard start to run dry. People started losing cohesion. Panic and desperation set in as it became clear that we were on our own now. People who went from a luxurious colonial life to one where death waits around every corner.

My men, the security force, were the first to step up. We had the guns, and what skills we could teach from our time in the military. But... No one is going to listen to the authorities. I'm honestly surprised we managed to even keep a hold on in the first place. The lot that didn't just up and leave were the hardest part of surviving. With so many mouths to feed, it was vital that we established hunters, gatherers, and farmers. We hunkered down near the crash site, just trying to train these people as best we could.

So many dead in the months after the crash. So many who just... broke. They couldn't handle it and... there was no room back then for someone who couldn't provide their hands. Those that refused to work, for any reason, had to be exiled to save on our dwindling food supplies. Sometimes I still wonder if some of those Brigands are the ones we exiled all those years ago.

Now? We might look like we've got something going on, but we really don't. We've tried our hardest to rebuild, but nature will just take it all from us anyways. The next generation will starve for it.

That's perhaps where you could come in. We've got something big planned. Something that could get us off this rock for good. If you want in, we'll get you a spot, but you'll have to do me a favor first.

There's a small fort holding what looks to be at least a hundred brigands. Our plans rely on our routes being clear of any threats, and they'll threaten everything we've been building up to. So I ran. Deep into the forest I well-knew was becoming home to an Abyssal force. I went on until I- I was here. Somewhere familiar yet- alien. There are an alien peoples called the Druflorans who've been found lingering on the edge of human-colonized space. Most colonial superpowers seldom interfere with primitive species these days given the political ramifications of invading and murdering these cultures, but- well, the smaller powers try anyways.

The Druflorans on the Razed planet have gained a significant leap in technology, effectively cheating cultural developments by a few hundred years. There seems to be two sides of what seems to be a continent-spanning conflict: a very asiatic culture, and a vaguely modern-militaristic rebel force.

This rebel force appears to be using, as far as we know, scrounged-up old colonial gear. We're seeing equipment that haven't seen proper use in hundreds of years. I have reason to believe this to be a result of attempted colonization attempts that underestimated the Drufloran's propensity to adapt and survive.

The asiatic culture is an interesting case. No such cases existed in the last 26 years, so they're an incredibly young civilization that somehow managed to cover over 2000 years of growth in that short time. This is the part that's curious, as they most resemble Shogunate-Era Japan. That's history over a thousand years ago, and I don't think any space power is going to be adopting muskets as their primary.

I need something from both sides. Documents, data tablets, maybe a manifesto from the asiatics. Anything that could tell us what's going on is probably going to be held by the military leaders of both sides.

And one more thing; don't rely too much on what you bring. Modern ammo is most likely going to be scarce, even from the militant rebels. Bring a blade as backup, alright? Good luck then.

Hello again. I have something to ask of you. Another service. It is hard for me to admit, but many years ago I made a grave mistake of smithing equipment for a human adventurer not unlike yourself, a man named Julian. He seemed to know exactly what I was, someone not properly human. He offered such a sizeable sum of currency and safe passage through his fiefdom that I admit to have so easily taken. In exchange, I was to craft him the finest armor in the lands. It scared me how confident he was.

I knew little of where I was, yet he prodded everything about me. From one world to the next, I was in a strange land I could only hope to survive in. Once he saw me demonstrate even the most basic of magic, he became ecstatic. He saw to the delivery of any kind of material I needed, even offering human sacrifices if that was what it took to 'make it work'. It disgusted me, but I couldn't just kill him. Where could I have gone? The workshop was the closest thing I had to home.

By the time I had finished smithing his armor, Julian seemed a little too... ecstatic. He paid in a few hefty bags of gold. I knew little of the land, but I could at least thank him for informing that even small pieces of gold could pay for a lot in these lands. But my nature as a youkai limited my true survival options. I needed something more primal to sustain myself. True fear. Julian had an unhealthy obsession with my powers, but I had more pressing concerns if I was to satiate my own growing hunger.

Word travelled fast. Julian had gone missing only a few weeks after my departure and his fiefdom had collapsed to petty power struggles. So I kept moving with what money I had left. No one was going to be friends with a 'terror' who scares their hearts out with illusion magic, so I kept moving around aimlessly, village-to-village. Was hard to stay disguised near people forever, though. My illusion magic can't change the colors of my eyes, and it's quite easy to recognize my red and blue.

^orange;Pristal shards^reset; are a crystal-metal hybrid that can be forged into ^orange;prisilite^reset;, which you can then make into some very shiny equipment. It's also one of the three components of tritanium alloy, so be sure to pick some up for that, if nothing else.
^orange;Telebrium^reset; is a crystal almost always found on moons, alongside erchius. It can conduct energy, but it's also strong against concussive force, so it's pretty versatile.

^orange;Lead^reset; poisoning is about the most mundane danger you'll be facing while you explore space - assuming you're a carbon lifeform, anyway - but do still be aware of it. Despite that, lead's super useful, especially for alloys, so do pick some up.
This is ^orange;irradium^reset;, and it makes your Geiger counter sing like an Avian! Its radioactivity can be made dormant, and it can then be made into some dangerous equipment, or strong alloys.

Among the many weird minerals of the universe, ^orange;sivite^reset; is surprisingly NOT one of the kinds you can make into wacky armor and weapons you won't ever get around to using. Rather, it's a nice source of magnesium powder and phosphorus if you extract it.
^orange;Protocite^reset; is only found on Proto Worlds. You can liquify it to power stuff, make it into alloys, or most importantly, make quantum computer chips from it.
That's pure ^orange;carbon^reset;. You can make it into carbon plating, or graphene, which are both great to have. Make sure to stock up on it if you can.

^orange;Cinnabar^reset; is a great source of mercury, if you extract it. This stuff, especially. It's actually very rare for it to be this pure! On Earth, anyway. The geology of the crazy planets we've been visiting might be a different case.
What you've just picked up is called ^orange;lasombrium^reset;, and it is a really creepy metal that phases in and out of reality, apparently. That is all the data I have on it.
That's ^orange;densinium^reset;! It is the toughest metal known to all of science, and it even glows purple, like the mythical, legendary ore it is. So cool...
^orange;Graphene^reset; is lovely stuff to have. It's used mostly as a capacitor to make advanced circuits, but it's also a great material to make equipment with.
^orange;Sulphur^reset; is useful for making fertilizers. It can also be extracted to get sulphuric acid, which is necessary for making batteries.
^orange;Magnesite^reset; is a great source of magnesium, if you smelt it or extract it. Magnesium is good to have for a fair few things, mostly involving biology.
^orange;Mascagnite^reset; is a good source of ammonium sulfate, if you extract it. 'Course, there's about a dozen other different ways to get it too...

That's ^orange;penumbrite^reset;, which is only found in penumbral biomes. Refine this stuff into shards, and you can craft some sleek equipment that looks the cool kind of alien. It's also useful for alloys, too.
^orange;Quietus^reset; is... well, it's, um, alive, kind of? I don't know, man. I guess you can still make it into stuff, but... Eugh...
^orange;Lunari^reset; is a particularly shiny breed of crystal. This stuff is everywhere on crystalline planets. If you refine it, you can make it into stuff just like you would a metal.
^orange;Zerchesium^reset; has an impressive melting point, so turn up the heat on your furnace if you plan to smelt it. You can use it to make advanced alloys, or a number of other neat things.
